title: Pagasa 13 mungbean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Pagasa 13 mungbean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Pagasa 13 mungbean is a mungbean variety. About 66 days to harvest, 1.5 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: Pagasa 13 is a registered mungbean variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2000 as NSIC 2000 Mg 08. It takes about 66 days from sowing to harvest, with 1.54 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

items: **Days to harvest:** about 66 days from sowing to harvest.
**Yield:** 1.54 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Pagasa 13 mungbean takes about 66 days from sowing to harvest. That is 6.2 days longer than the average of the 33 mungbean varieties with a day count, 59.8 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.54 t/ha beats the average of its group, 1.25. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It was weak against cercospora leaf spot, so scout for it from the early weeks. Read up on [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot).

The pests and diseases that hit mungbean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 6.4 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed coat is glossy green. The seed holds 24.02 percent crude protein.
Where and when to plant Pagasa 13 mungbean

Munggo is ready in about two months, so it fits the gap after rice. Pick a variety that ripens its pods together, which saves picking rounds, and one rated against cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 66 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.54 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Pagasa 13?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
